subject: On-prem deployment — evidence/access safeguards and MSA/Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@medifold.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Pat O'Neil <pat.oneil@vendorlaw.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on on-prem evidence & operator access (MSA/Order Form)

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our security team reviewed the MSA and the proposed Order Form for the on-prem deployment. We have a few open items before we can present to leadership: 

- Can you confirm the exact scope of license rights when the runtime is installed in our datacenter (are backups/snapshots explicitly covered, and what about failover copies)?
- We need an evidence-handling proposal similar to an escrow-lite workflow — specifically, how would Redwood provide snapshot verification or forensic access in a jurisdictionally segmented environment?
- For operator access: we need to understand temporary access windows for debug/audit and whether that requires a signed Exhibit or short-term MSA carveout.

I attached a brief list of the technical evidence the security team expects (see evidence-checklist.xlsx). We'd appreciate a concise set of redline proposals that we can route to our legal team.

Proposed timeline: we'd like to lock terms by 10 May to meet our deployment window. Can you confirm if that's realistic?

Best,
Elena Cruz
Director, Vendor Management — MediFold Systems

Attachment: evidence-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet — checklists of snapshots, timestamping, witnessing)
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@medifold.com>, procurement@medifold.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on on-prem evidence & operator access (MSA/Order Form)

Elena — thank you, and great questions. Quick summary up front: 

- License scope: Redwood's standard on-prem annex grants use rights for running the licensed runtime and associated artifacts for the agreed residency instance; we cover backups/snapshots used for DR within the same jurisdiction as part of the runtime license, but we do track exhibit language for long-term archival copies.
- Evidence/escrow-lite: we can propose a two-tier model — (1) signed snapshot notarization with hash verification delivered over SFTP or a secure Drive link, and (2) time-limited witness access under an agreed exhibit for forensic validation.
- Operator access: temporary console/SSH access is possible for specific windows; we propose a 72-hour maximum per incident with explicit logging, one-time keys, and customer approval for each window.

I'm looping in David (legal) and Dylan (Infra Eng) to draft specific redlines for the MSA Appendix and the Order Form Exhibit. I'll attach our initial redline pack in the next reply so you have text to take to Pat.

Thanks — we'll aim to have draft redlines and an Order Form exhibit by EOD tomorrow so you can begin internal review. If the 10 May target is firm, please flag now and we'll prioritize.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Operations Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none in this message)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@medifold.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on on-prem evidence & operator access (MSA/Order Form)

Elena / Neha / team — attaching a proposed set of redlines (Redlines_MSA_v3.docx) and a draft Order Form (OrderForm_MediFold.pdf). Key highlights of our proposed language: 

1) License scope: insert new Section 2.3(a)(v) — "Snapshots and DR copies created as part of the licensed runtime operation are licensed to Customer for internal business use; transfer or redistribution outside Customer's controlled environments requires Customer notice and separate license."

2) Evidence-handling Exhibit (Exhibit F): Redwood will provide hash-signed snapshot bundles and a validation report. For jurisdictional constraints, Redwood will store encrypted snapshot digests in a mutually accessible storage location and provide a signed attestation upon request.

3) Operator access window: new Exhibit G — emergency access protocol. Access limited to 72 hours per incident, requires written escalation approval (email), multi-factor single-use credentials, and the ability for Customer to revoke at any time. All sessions are logged and delivered to Customer after the window.

4) Audit/witnessing: where witness certification is required, Redwood will offer two options — remote witnessed verification or in-person notarized handoff. Costs for travel/witnessing are out-of-scope unless requested.

Open items we need MediFold to confirm: (i) whether you require a recurring snapshot deposit cadence (e.g., weekly) and (ii) whether you require witness certification language to be mandatory vs. optional.

Pat — please chime in on the redline approach; we tried to keep the exhibit modular so it can be appended to the Order Form without altering core MSA indemnities.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redlines_MSA_v3.docx (redline track changes), OrderForm_MediFold.pdf
From: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@medifold.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Pat O'Neil <pat.oneil@vendorlaw.com>, procurement@medifold.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on on-prem evidence & operator access (MSA/Order Form)

David / Neha — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear redlines. A few clarifying points from our security/legal: 

- Snapshot cadence: security prefers weekly deposits for production clusters, with a 90-day retention minimum for the snapshot hash digests.
- Witnessing: we'd like witness verification to be an included option in Exhibit F (not mandatory), but we need language that Redwood will not object to the order form if witness verification is selected by Customer.
- Operator access revocation: please confirm that revocation is immediate and that session logs are delivered within 48 hours after termination.

Two small asks: can you indicate in the Order Form the expected SLA impact (if any) during an access window, and include a short example of the rollback procedure in Exhibit F so our ops people can triage the steps? 

We are preparing an internal memo for leadership on Monday — if possible, could you move the redlines to DocuSign by the end of day Monday so our counsel can execute on Tuesday?

Best,
Elena

Elena — quick update and next steps. David and Jordan incorporated your notes: weekly snapshot deposit + 90-day hash retention included as an option in Exhibit F; witness verification remains optional but with mandatory non-objection language. Operator access revocation is immediate; logs delivered within 24–48 hours (we'll commit to 48 hours in the exhibit).

Jordan (infra) added a short rollback example to Exhibit F and a short SLA note indicating no intended SLA degradation for short access windows (we'll call out escalation and fallback models if a prolonged engineering engagement is required).

Next steps: 
- I've uploaded the final redline package to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-evidence (same link above).
- If that looks good, we'll send the Order Form and Exhibit as an execution packet via DocuSign here: https://docusign.com/send/0a1b2c3d.
- Proposed 30-min call to lock the cadence and witness preferences: Tue 4 May, 11:00–11:30 PT. Please confirm availability.

If you confirm the 11:00 slot, we'll mark the DocuSign packet for review afterward so Pat/your counsel can sign Wednesday. We'll aim to keep the 10 May target intact.

Thanks — looking forward.
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
